title: Corran Vey, a veteran of the Drum, at the cottage door
description: The first companion offers to walk with the player (375 S17). A veteran from the Drum, a kind of person the reference describes; never one of the book's cast. Placeholder name and lines.
speaker: Corran Vey

door.text: Morning. Don't get up. Name's Corran Vey; I stood twenty years in the Drum before my knees gave out. They're saying at the well you held Harrow's house against the eyeless ones, alone, through a night with no moon.

choices.text: Not quite alone. Wenlan had a poker.

laugh.text: Ha. Good man, Harrow. Still. Whatever comes up out of the dark comes again, and a pike at your flank is worth two at your back.

choices.text: You're offering to come with me?

offer.text: I'm too old to farm and too stubborn to sit. You go looking where the eyeless ones went; I'll take their flank while you take their front. Neck or heart, isn't it? I remember.

danger.text: Twenty years in the Drum. I know what dangerous is. Now, are we walking?

join.text: Lead on. I'll keep a step behind, and closer when it counts.
